title: New Zealand Accredited Employer Visa 2026: Singapore Guide
metaDescription: New Zealand Accredited Employer Work Visa 2026 for Singapore applicants: 30-hour job offer, NZ$23.95 wage floor, 2-year experience rule, maximum stay.
headline: New Zealand Accredited Employer Visa 2026: Singapore Guide

sections.title: What is the Accredited Employer Work Visa?
sections.content:
The Accredited Employer Work Visa, or AEWV, is New Zealand's main temporary work visa for skilled workers with a genuine job offer. It links the worker directly to an employer that Immigration New Zealand has accredited, and the specific role must pass an approved job check before the worker applies.

The system has three stages: employer accreditation, a job check for the role, and then the migrant's own visa application. Each stage is assessed separately, so a job offer alone is not enough; the employer and the role must both be approved first.

sections.title: Core requirements for workers
sections.content:
Workers need a full-time job offer of at least 30 hours per week from an accredited employer, paying at least the market rate for the role and location, and at least the adult minimum wage of NZ$23.95 per hour from 1 April 2026. They also need either two years of relevant work experience or a relevant qualification at NZQCF Level 4 or higher.

Health and character checks are mandatory, including police certificates and, for longer stays, medical certificates and chest X-rays. Applicants should gather employment evidence early, because gaps in work history are a common cause of delays and requests for more information.

sections.title: English and maximum stay rules
sections.content:
English evidence is required for jobs at skill level 3, 4 or 5, with IELTS 4.0 overall commonly cited, alongside alternatives such as PTE Academic 29 or TOEFL iBT 31. Skill level 1 and 2 jobs generally have no English requirement, although employers may still set their own language expectations for the role.

Maximum stay is five years for skill level 1 to 3 jobs and some other eligible roles, and three years for other skill level 4 and 5 jobs, followed by 12 months outside New Zealand before a further AEWV in many cases. Residence pathways exist for some roles, including Green List and Work to Residence routes.

sections.title: Costs, documents and how to apply
sections.content:
The AEWV fee starts from NZ$1,540, and most straightforward applications are decided within about five to six weeks, although complex cases take longer. Required documents include a signed job offer and employment agreement, a job description, qualification or experience evidence, and, where required, English results and police certificates.

Apply only through Immigration New Zealand's official online system, and be wary of anyone promising a guaranteed visa for cash. Rules change frequently, so confirm the current requirements on immigration.govt.nz or with a licensed immigration adviser before paying fees or resigning from a job.

faqs.q: How many hours must an AEWV job offer cover?
faqs.a: An AEWV job offer must be full-time, meaning at least 30 hours per week, from an employer accredited by Immigration New Zealand, with an approved job check for that specific role. The job must pay at least the market rate and the adult minimum wage, and the offer must still be current when you apply.

faqs.q: What experience or qualification do you need for an AEWV?
faqs.a: Applicants generally need two years of relevant work experience or a relevant qualification at NZQCF Level 4 or higher, unless an exemption applies. Evidence should clearly match the offered role, because Immigration New Zealand checks that your skills and experience fit the job described in the approved job check.

faqs.q: Do you need English for an AEWV?
faqs.a: English evidence is required for jobs at skill level 3, 4 or 5, for example IELTS 4.0 overall, PTE Academic 29 or TOEFL iBT 31, with results no more than two years old. Skill level 1 and 2 jobs generally have no English requirement under the visa rules, although an employer may still expect English for the work itself.

faqs.q: How long can you stay on an AEWV?
faqs.a: Maximum stay is five years for skill level 1 to 3 jobs and some other eligible roles, and three years for other skill level 4 and 5 jobs, followed in many cases by 12 months outside New Zealand. Some roles can lead to residence through Green List or Work to Residence pathways, depending on pay and occupation.
